title: Concurrency vs parallelism: what's the difference?
hook: What is the difference between concurrency and parallelism?
lines: What is the difference between concurrency and parallelism?
Concurrency is one cook switching between two dishes: stir one, then chop for the other.
Only one thing happens at any instant, but both dishes make progress.
Parallelism is two cooks, each working on their own dish at the very same time.
Concurrency is about dealing with many things at once.
Parallelism is about doing many things at once.
So concurrency is how you structure the work, and parallelism is how it runs.
subject: concurrency vs parallelism
